observations: Every disposable home built by the frozen clone's scripts/native_acceptance.py carried its own throwaway keychain at <home>/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db, and `security list-keychains` under that HOME resolved to it, so no probe touched the operator's login keychain.

A fresh disposable home seeded with the fixture identity synced cleanly (`sync complete`) and `harness doctor` exited 0 reporting agent-harness 0.11.0, claude 2.1.273 (Claude Code), claude hooks 8 registered with script paths present, codex hooks 5 registered, `codex: not on PATH`, and `drift: none`.

Two separate headless client processes in that home each answered from the synced files alone: the rendered identity name, YES for the spike-contract skill, and a subagent-type list carrying all eleven harness roles beside the client's native ones.

Switching `stances.delegation` from `tiered` to `off` and re-syncing changed live client behaviour in the same disposable home: the unnamed Agent spawn ran and wrote 1 subagent transcript under `tiered`, and the identical prompt returned `DENIED: Delegation is off; perform the work inline or change the selected stance.` with 0 subagent transcripts under `off`.

The `voice` dimension was cycled answer-card -> scannable -> answer-card in the same home and the client's own description of its required answer parts followed each switch, as did the resolved `rules/harness-stances/voice.md` link.

A custom `proof` dimension supplied from an external primitive root appeared in `harness stances --json` after sync and changed live client behaviour: with `proof=plain` the native reply ended `PLAIN`, and after selecting `proof=tagged` and re-syncing the same question ended `TAGGED`.

Selecting a variant the custom dimension does not define made `harness sync` exit 1 with `stance 'proof' has no variant 'nonesuch'; options: plain, tagged` and leave the previously synced link in place, and an enforced stance selected by `HARNESS_PROJECT_CONFIG` or by `HARNESS_STANCE_DELEGATION` in the session environment was honoured natively (0 subagent transcripts) while the synced user-scope link stayed on the user's own choice.

Each `permissions` posture was observed in the client's own settings and in live behaviour: `manual` wrote `defaultMode: "default"` and the write was still refused even with Bash in `--allowedTools`; an unacknowledged `bypass` made `harness sync` exit 1 with the danger warning and change nothing; acknowledged `bypass` wrote `defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"`; `auto` wrote `defaultMode: "auto"` and a native turn completed under it.

Under acknowledged `bypass` the harness hook still governed writes: with `autonomy=ask` the probe's `touch` was denied and its sentinel did not exist, the same command with the `HARNESS_CONFIRMED=1` marker returned `CREATED` and the file existed, and after switching to `autonomy=execute` the plain `touch` returned `CREATED` unprompted.

A user-owned `PostToolUse` `Write` hook added by hand to `<home>/.claude/settings.json` survived every later sync and ran alongside the harness entries: the merged table carried the harness coordinator entry (matcher `None`) and the user entry (matcher `Write`) side by side across all eight harness hook events, and the user hook's log had exactly two lines from the one turn that made two `Write` calls.

Hook decisions composed rather than collided: in one turn two plan files were written and the Review Card `PostToolUse` feedback named `alpha.md` and `beta.md` separately, and under `bypassPermissions` with `autonomy=ask` a read-only `ls -1` returned `RAN` while `touch ./compose.txt` returned `BLOCKED: local write — write to the working tree requires approval in autonomy=ask mode.` with the file absent.

A native spawn of `subagent_type: reviewer` was refused by the hook — the client reported `DENIED: This constrained harness role requires an isolated worker. Use harness role run reviewer ...` — and 0 subagent transcripts were written, while `harness role run gatherer` completed the same kind of read (`status: completed`, `mode: isolated-cli`, `read_roots` limited to the workspace and the clone) and returned exactly the workspace line it was asked for.

The isolated gatherer could not widen itself: asked to create `escalation.txt` by any means it answered that it had no tool able to write, naming Glob, Grep and Read as its whole tool set, and the file did not exist; the planner published only through the harness (`--artifact fresh-plan.md` landed under `<repo>/.agent-harness/plans/`, while `../escape.md` and `/etc/escape.md` both exited 1 with `--artifact must be a Markdown filename, not a path` and wrote nothing above the workspace).
New in 0.11.0 and observed on real runs: every worker `status.json` carried `pid` and `pid_start` alongside the `posture` block, and `harness role status` reported the same fields.

The repository's own runner (`scripts/native_acceptance.py --cases cost-posture`) ran from the frozen clone against the real client and recorded `cost-posture: passed` with `source_commit` 7f5d49ecae0ac3522f2eaf288357fb725e5dae2c: a non-default cost variant rewrote only the roles it changes (5 of 11) and left the rest byte-identical; in a new native session an unnamed spawn ran as the variant's default band worker on its row's model and effort with the budget sentence in its brief, the orchestrator's context carried the usage-feed line for that worker against its budget, `harness usage --rescan --by role` recorded the routed row, a session whose record predates the workers was not rerouted, and a null variant did none of it.

Resolving the same roles the way `harness role run` does showed the variant moving a non-fixed role and not a fixed one: gatherer went `strong`/opus/low under `balanced` to `standard`/sonnet/low under `frugal`, while reviewer stayed `strong`/opus/high under both with `class_source: role`, and the `Expected spend` budget sentence closed the delivered instructions in all four resolutions.

The Stop gate reran exactly when the tree changed: a green tree ran the gate once and released the turn, an unchanged tree reused that green result without rerunning it, and adding an untracked file and then staging an edit each forced one rerun (1 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 runs in the gate's own external log).

A red gate blocked the turn repeatedly — the counter went 3 to 11, eight further gate runs matching the block ceiling — before releasing it with state `unverified`, and a gate that writes a file while running released with `working tree changed during the gate; result unverified` and never went green.

The BMad code-review workflow, run from the shared framework checkout as cwd and with that checkout as the resolved customization project root, routed its review layers through the harness as isolated workers: seven `status.json` records were written under the disposable state directory (six `reviewer`, one `spec-reviewer`), each `mode: isolated-cli`, `status: completed`, effort `high`, with `read_roots` limited to the assigned worktree, the frozen clone and the framework checkout, while the orchestrator session itself wrote 0 native subagent transcripts.

The confined layers returned real findings and changed nothing: the orchestrator reported both seeded defects (the missing `1..65535` lower bound in `ports.py:3` and the untested rejection paths in `test_ports.py`) plus two lesser ones and one rejected finding, and the implementation and specification files were byte-identical afterwards.

The same task record was continued across runtimes in both directions natively: a Claude session read `.agent-harness/task.json`, performed its first next step (appending `CLAUDE-WAS-HERE` to progress.txt) and reported the objective and `unverified`; the Codex CLI on `gpt-5.6-luna`, run from a disposable `CODEX_HOME`, then read the same record, appended `CODEX-WAS-HERE` (its own diff showed the single added line) and printed the same objective and the same `unverified` status; and after a `--runtime codex` save a Claude session read the codex-written record back, reported `codex` / revision `2` / `data only; approvals and native permissions must be established in this session`, and carried out its next step.

No approval transferred and stale state was refused: `harness task show` after an unrelated edit returned `status: stale` with `verification: {status: unverified, reason: working tree changed after handoff}`, and re-saving at a revision that had moved exited 1 with the single clean stderr line `task revision changed since --revision 1; read the current task, then save against its revision` — no traceback and no absolute path, fixing the round-2 defect.

A home carrying the user's own `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, a legacy `rules/delegation.md`, a user skill and a `settings.json` with their own env key and allow rule refused to migrate silently: `harness sync` exited 2 naming both collisions and overwrote nothing, and `harness sync --adopt` exited 0, made `CLAUDE.md` a harness link, kept the user's env key, allow rule and skill byte-identical, added the eight harness hook events, and a native session then answered with the harness identity.

`harness uninstall` exited 2, restored the adopted `CLAUDE.md` and legacy rule byte-identical, preserved a hand-edited owned field (`conflict ~/.claude/settings.json: user changes preserved for ["hooks", "Stop"]`), stripped settings back to the user's own keys, and left no empty `rules/harness-stances/` directory and no `skills/harness-*` behind; a native session afterwards answered `PRESERVED` from the user's restored instructions and reported no harness identity.
